summary: Most trend tools draw a line through noise and print a p-value. Trend Detective is built to refuse them. It pulls five real variables from NASA POWER (MERRA-2 temperature, precipitation and soil wetness; CERES albedo and shortwave) for any region and any time window, then applies three mandatory gates — a block-permutation null that preserves autocorrelation, a Mann-Kendall test corrected with Hamed-Rao effective sample size, and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery control — before it is allowed to report a trend. If the signal does not clear the gates it returns NO VERDICT, together with the smallest trend the record could actually detect. It also answers 'where': a per-cell slope field with FDR-significance, which on the Sahel shows 16 cells rising and 28 falling inside one region. Live at https://trend.mawqi3k.com/
details: What it does. A region-selectable dashboard over NASA Earth data. For every variable it reports a Theil-Sen slope with a permutation confidence interval, a Hamed-Rao corrected Mann-Kendall p-value, a Benjamini-Hochberg q-value, detrended anomaly years, a linear projection with widening uncertainty, and a per-cell spatial slope field whose significance is FDR-controlled. Four regions are pre-loaded (Western Sahel, Jordan Badia, Arctic tundra, Gobi Desert) and any bounding box can be analysed live. A window switch recomputes everything on 1981-2023 or 2001-2023. How it works. A dependency-free C++17 engine (trend-detect) computes the statistics and prints its own calibration on demand: 3.8% false positives over 600 synthetic series, with detection rising from 0.17 to 0.93 as the slope grows. A zero-dependency Node server exposes the engine as JSON and fetches custom regions from the NASA POWER API. The front end is hand-written HTML/CSS/JS with SVG charts and a locally vendored Leaflet map over NASA GIBS imagery. Benefits and impact. Anyone can interrogate the numbers the way a scientist would. Every claim carries p, q, the effective sample size and the detection limit, and NO VERDICT is reported rather than hidden when the gates are not passed. The most useful number in the project is the detection limit: it tells a student, journalist or planner when a dashboard should stay silent. The interface is bilingual English/Arabic with full RTL support. Creativity factors considered. Showing that a conclusion can depend on the record window (Sahel temperature is -0.32 C per decade on 2001-2023 and +0.15 C per decade on 1981-2023), controlling the false discovery rate across 45 spatial cells, and refusing to report trends that the data cannot support. Tools used. C++17 (portable build), Node.js 20, vanilla JavaScript and SVG, Leaflet 1.9.4 (vendored, BSD-2), Docker, nginx with Let's Encrypt TLS, NASA POWER (MERRA-2 and CERES SYN1deg) and NASA GIBS.
